contract: The Python and TypeScript SDKs expose export_log as a read-only audit collection whose model matches the canonical PostgreSQL table.
findings: The prior SDK create payload named format, entity_type, entity_ids, and requested_by, none of which exist in the canonical export_log table.
The repository's exporter writes completed audit rows after it generates files; no worker consumes pending export_log rows.
export_log status, file metadata, and row counts are generated by the exporter and must not be caller-mutated through the SDK.
change: Removed export-log create, bulk-create, update, and delete methods from both SDKs; retained list/get and aligned the ExportLog model fields to the ten canonical table columns. Export generation remains available through services.export.exporter.
scope_limits: All HTTP transports were mocked; no database, provider, candidate, or legacy service was used.
This does not implement an authenticated Gateway export-request queue or asynchronous export worker.
The capability matrix classifications and MAN-CAP acceptance remain unchanged.
rollback: Revert the SDK method/type/README and test changes. Reintroduce SDK mutations only after an additive schema contract, authenticated Gateway authorization and attribution, and durable request processing are implemented and tested.
